auditMethod: Read-only inspection of saved JSON, raw diagnostic logs, archived diagnostic sources, classifier code, and the installed websocket dependency. No socket, Go, SDK, or load execution.

baseline.unclassifiedLimit: The 12 baseline rows labeled unclassified_or_real_deadline all have no client read_end and no elapsed write deadline or deadline error. All are designated slow readers. The label does not demonstrate any real deadline failure.

limits: Use the 27 read-cancel and 13 explicit-close categories as the exclusive classification. The 35 close-before-error timing observations overlap 22 read-cancel rows.
The diagnostic source has no read_sleep_cancel log. Do not claim such an event was captured.
This is an additional execution with a timing discrepancy. Use its per-connection abort/write-error evidence for causality, not performance.

clocks.measurementClockSource: The archived load source calculates the rate denominator using time.Since(started), retaining Go monotonic time. The measurementSeconds report field is the configured duration.
clocks.discrepancyCause: Unknown. The saved evidence cannot distinguish a wall-clock adjustment, host suspend behavior, or another cause.
clocks.interpretation: The whole wall interval includes setup, warmup, measurement, and cleanup, so it is not directly the same interval as the Go measurement. The 3617.815506-second wall interval nevertheless does not support an uninterrupted 15-second wall-clock trial. Near-cleanup event order, dependency behavior, and matching counters support the abort mechanism; do not infer workload duration, stable performance, or suspend cause from this extra diagnostic.

historical139.limit: Original139counter increments lacked per-event strings; this proves the same-source same-profile reproduced mechanism, not a one-to-one retrospective mapping.
historical139.wording: The original 139 increments lack per-event error strings and cannot be assigned a retrospective one-to-one cause. Same-profile retests of the prior implementation with diagnostic logging reproduced the cancellation/abrupt-close mechanism. Instrumentation and scheduling can change the count.

normalProtocolScope: These diagnostics use read-context cancellation followed by CloseNow and do not send Leave. They demonstrate abrupt transport shutdown, not successful Leave/Left/close-1000 protocol shutdown. Claims about normal protocol shutdown need the separate protocol tests and final Left/normal-closure counts.
suggestedReportWording: The six prior profiles reproduced 178 post-measurement write errors: 144, 1, 9, 9, 14, and 1. Setup and measurement rate, queue, and write-error deltas were zero; all six fail the full-lifecycle zero-error gate.

Tracing associates 166 errors with canceled client reads. The 12 remaining baseline errors are slow-reader broken pipes before the server write deadline. An additional diagnostic records all 13 slow readers closing their sockets before their associated server write errors; its exclusive totals are 27 read cancellations and 13 explicit socket closes.

The extra diagnostic has a 3617.815506-second whole wall interval and a 15.5482195-second Go measurement interval. The discrepancy cause is unknown. Its event traces support the shutdown mechanism only; performance results use the separately recorded final runs.
These executions do not recover the individual causes of the historical 139 increments. They distinguish abrupt client shutdown from the normal Leave/Left/close-1000 flow.
